Assessment updated with Beige Book:
- The June 2017 FOMC action (hike to 1–1.25% and signaling gradual balance-sheet normalization) is moderately hawkish.
- May 2017 Beige Book points to modest-to-moderate growth with broad but incremental job gains; labor markets are tight and wages are rising mainly for skilled workers, while overall wage/price pressures remain modest. Housing demand generally outpaced a softer commercial real estate backdrop (notably retail), and tourism activity supported growth in several districts. Energy-sector conditions improved, aiding activity in related regions. Lending volumes broadly mirrored the modest expansion.
- Together with the April SLOOS showing tighter standards for auto and parts of CRE and some softening in credit demand, these reports temper the hawkish signal from the statement by highlighting subdued inflation pressures and selective sectoral softness.

Net: still moderately hawkish, but Beige Book and SLOOS slightly soften the tone versus a statement-only read.
